chunks: Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from Muhammad ibn Murazim, from his father, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
When the crescent moon forms a complete encirclement, it is for two nights, and when you see the shadow of your head in it, it is for three nights.

key_terms.تَطَوَّقَ: To encircle or form a complete circle
key_terms.لِثَلَاثِ لَيَالٍ: For the three nights (implying 30 days total)
key_terms.لِلَّيْلَتَيْنِ: For the two nights (implying 29 days total)

ai.seo_question: How to determine if a lunar month has 29 or 30 days based on the crescent moon?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi outlines the astronomical criteria for determining the length of lunar months, specifically distinguishing between a 29-day month (indicated by a fully encirced crescent) and a 30-day month (indicated by the visibility of one's head's shadow). It reflects the Shia scholarly reliance on visual observation (ru'yah) combined with precise celestial mechanics to establish the beginning of fasting and Eid, ensuring alignment with the Prophet's tradition.

en.hubeali:
Ahmad Bin Idrees, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Yaqoub Bin Yazeed, from Muhammad Bin Murazim, from his father, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘When the crescent forms (a visible) encirclement, so it is for the second night, and when you see the shadow of your head in it, so it is for the third night (of that month)’.
en.sarwar: 11. Ahmad ibn Idris Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Ya’qub ibn Yazid from Muhammad ibn Murazim from his father who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
if the crescent forms a crown around it, then it is two nights old and if you can see the shadow of your head it is three nights old.’”
